About me

Who I am

  • Madrid, Spain
  • Available to start immediately

Welcome, and thanks for taking an interest in my profile and projects. I'm Alejandro Tejero, a Telecommunications Engineer specialized in Telematics from Universidad Rey Juan Carlos. Honestly, a few years ago I wouldn't have bet on getting this far. I was never the best at anything, but my effort made things go relatively well for me. When I started the degree and saw how demanding it was, I knew I had two paths: really start pushing myself, knowing the sacrifices and changes that would take, or change direction. I chose the first, and today I know it was the right call. As the saying goes, those four years turned into the best five, and that's where I truly learned that nothing worthwhile comes without effort, and that if you want to aim high, hard work alone isn't enough - you also need to handle pressure, stay organized, and never back down.

Getting through the degree often meant putting study or work ahead of plans anyone would rather be doing. That taught me something very clear: your future depends, above all, on you. The most important thing is knowing your goals, your objectives and your dreams - once you have that clear, organization and hard work follow almost on their own.

After finishing my degree, I did my internship at Robert Bosch España, where I analyzed production data, designed databases and built tracking dashboards in Power BI and SAP. It was my first real contact with a large, demanding work environment, and it's where I realized I like doing things properly, understanding why they're done a certain way, and paying attention to detail. I now follow that same approach investigating and building my own projects, and training myself in areas like networking, cybersecurity, cloud, data and AI. For me, learning doesn't end with the degree - technology never stops moving forward, and I'm a curious person besides, so continuing to learn isn't an obligation, it's something I enjoy.

Talks

July 6, 2026

1st Conference on Free Software and Open AI (seLIA)

Speaker

URJC campus de Fuenlabrada

When I defended my thesis, WebBuilder, my professors invited me to take part in the 1st Conference on Free Software and Open AI (seLIA), on the URJC Fuenlabrada campus. I submitted my proposal to the organizers and it was received better than I expected, with a lot of interest in the project. The conference brought together 38 talks and workshops spread across several rooms throughout the day, so I got to attend sessions on very different topics: from deploying local AI models without relying on external providers, to debates on how to regulate free software, to the risks of the unchecked productivity of vibe coding. I had given presentations before, but this one felt different. It felt like the audience recognising an effort that usually goes unseen, and it put a fitting close to a stage of my life that was hard but also beautiful, one I look back on with very good memories.
